problems.title: Long or short vol?
problems.solution: Long options are long gamma and vega; short options are short both.

problems.title: Hedged P&L
problems.statement: Long an ATM option with Γ = 0.05, S = 100; the stock moves 2% in a day; implied 20% (daily variance (0.2/√252)²).

problems.title: Implied vol
problems.statement: A one-year ATM call (S = K = 100, r = 0) trades at 12.

parts.prompt: Implied vol by the ATM rule (C/(0.4 S √T))?

problems.title: Skew
problems.statement: Equity index 90%-strike puts trade at higher implied vol than ATM options.
problems.solution: The skew prices the tails and the dynamics Black–Scholes leaves out.

problems.title: Vega P&L
problems.statement: Vega = 0.40 per vol point; implied vol rises from 20% to 23%.

problems.title: Selling vol
problems.statement: Selling options earns a premium most months but loses heavily in crashes.

parts.prompt: Which earlier lesson does this echo?
options: the doubling strategy: frequent small wins, rare large losses

problems.solution: A high hit rate with a fat left tail: judge it by expected value and tail risk.

problems.title: Realised vs implied
problems.statement: You buy a 1-year option at 18% implied and hedge continuously; volatility realises at 24%. Using the rough total P&L ≈ vega × (σ_r − σ_i) with vega 0.40 per point.
hints: Hedged long option ≈ long realised minus implied.
problems.solution: About +2.40 (path-dependent in reality: it depends on where gamma was large when the moves happened).
